runs.text: Rocket's unsecured leverage has fallen to a moderate level, but the improvement is earnings-led and the latest ratio is the first on a clean base. Senior notes of USD 10,743 million (principal) stand at 3.78x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,843 million and 2.83x net of USD 2,699 million of cash, against 8.16x for FY2025 and 5.65x at March 31, 2026, when earnings held only part of the Mr. Cooper business while debt already held its assumed notes. Principal rose from USD 10,455 million at December 31, 2025, so deleveraging came from earnings, not repayment [CP-1 leverage table; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on cause].

The ratio flatters the forward position. Adjusted revenue fell from USD 2,822 million in Q1 2026 to USD 2,761 million in Q2 2026 and USD 2,574 million in Q3 2026, and the company guides Q4 2026 to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion, below each quarter in the last-twelve-month window. The third quarter coincided with a 30-year mortgage rate that rose from 6.43% to 7.28% and a smaller market, while GAAP net income of USD 709 million included an MSR valuation gain that the company strips out of adjusted measures. Creditors should anchor on adjusted EBITDA with that caveat and treat the 3.78x as a trailing, not forward, figure [CP-1; CP-1A].

Rocket's funding has two layers that behave differently. The unsecured layer, senior notes and an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver maturing in 2029, has no maturity before the USD 503 million convertible in April 2027, then USD 1,500 million in 2029, USD 2,076 million in 2030 and USD 2,214 million in 2031. The secured layer of USD 14,187 million sits on lines whose committed amount is USD 7,400 million, with USD 10,295 million outstanding on lines dated 2027 and USD 3,462 million on lines dated 2028. Rocket therefore faces recurring renewal and margin-call risk on warehouse capacity even though its bond maturity profile is long, and most facilities carry cross default or cross acceleration terms [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact].

Liquidity is real but partly unverified. The company states total liquidity of USD 11.4 billion, of which only USD 2,699 million of cash and the USD 2,500 million revolver tie to the filings; the USD 6.2 billion of undrawn available MSR and advance lines cannot be reproduced from the facility table, and cash includes buy-down and margin cash that are not quantified. Stated liquidity is management data and should be attributed as such [CP-1; Management Language].

The servicing franchise is the most durable source of revenue and also a concentration. Servicing fee income was USD 3,181 million in the nine months of 2026 on a portfolio of USD 2,007,176 million of unpaid principal, with 60-plus day delinquency of 1.52%. The Agencies and subservicing clients can terminate servicing with little or no notice, and MSRs of USD 20,257 million at fair value are the largest balance sheet asset and are valued with rate and prepayment assumptions. A change in Agency terms or an MSR valuation reversal would hit income, collateral value for the MSR lines and liquidity at once [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact].

Control and sponsor behaviour matter because protections are not visible. Mr. Gilbert holds more than a majority of the voting power, the company relies on controlled company exemptions and renounces certain corporate opportunities in favour of RHI II parties. Documented capital actions are mixed: a USD 120.1 million special dividend in 2025, withdrawal of undrawn related party credit lines, equity-funded acquisitions and no distributions in the 2026 cash flow statements. Nothing in the pack shows the restricted payment, lien or guarantee terms that would limit owner actions [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on overall category].

Event risk is concentrated in litigation and acquired liabilities. Legal reserves rose to USD 216 million from USD 74 million, acquisition accounting added USD 100 million of litigation and regulatory accruals in Q3 2026, and a USD 175 million HouseCanary verdict against Rocket Close awaits judgment while the plaintiff is in Chapter 11. A judgment above facility thresholds that is not paid, bonded or stayed could default funding facilities, which links a legal outcome to liquidity [CP-1 claims outside funded debt; Documentary Fact].

Earnings carry adjustments and a definition that favours the headline. Adjusted EBITDA is after secured financing interest but before bond interest, adds back USD 291 million of acquisition-related expenses and USD 338 million of acquired intangible amortization in the nine months, and removes an MSR valuation gain of USD 852 million. Accrual cover of last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA over bond interest is 4.94x, and cash interest cover is available only for FY2025 at 2.15x on a mixed basis. Debt service capacity therefore rests on an accrual proxy and on adjusted rather than reported earnings [CP-1 earnings quality; Analyst Interpretation].

Market pricing of the unsecured notes weakened over the period. The aggregate fair value of senior notes of USD 10,258 million at September 30, 2026 was below carrying value of USD 10,716 million, whereas at December 31, 2025 fair value of USD 10,502 million was above carrying value of USD 10,423 million, and the weighted average interest rate on the notes rose to 5.43% from 5.03%. This is an aggregate, not a tranche-level price, and ratings are not supplied [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on direction].

runs.text: Scaled servicing and origination franchise [Documentary Fact]. Rocket Companies, Inc. services USD 2,007,176 million of unpaid principal, earned USD 3,181 million of servicing fee income in the nine months of 2026 and closed USD 43.6 billion of loans in Q3 2026. Recurring servicing fees support revenue visibility through a rate cycle better than origination alone, and the portfolio's 60-plus day delinquency of 1.52% is stable against 1.50% at year end [CP-1A operating model].

Moderate unsecured leverage on a full earnings base [Documentary Fact]. Gross 3.78x and net 2.83x on last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, with accrual bond interest cover of 4.94x, give room to absorb some earnings decline before leverage reaches the 5.65x seen at March 31, 2026 [CP-1 leverage table; Analyst Interpretation on headroom].

Long unsecured maturity profile and an undrawn revolver [Documentary Fact]. No note matures before April 2027, the largest annual maturities fall in 2031 and 2033, and the USD 2,500 million revolver is undrawn and runs to 2029, which gives the issuer time and a committed buffer [CP-1 debt maturities; CP-1 liquidity table].

Equity-funded growth [Documentary Fact]. Redfin and Mr. Cooper were bought for stock, with cash of USD 252 million and USD 3,113 million used to settle target debt, so the acquisitions did not require a new debt-funded purchase price. Equity of USD 24,311 million and equity less goodwill and intangibles of USD 11,745 million (a consolidated proxy, not a covenant measure) provide loss-absorbing capital for the debt [CP-1A transactions; CP-1 financials].

Stated compliance [Documentary Fact]. The company states compliance with all funding covenants and with agency net worth, liquidity and capital ratio requirements at September 30, 2026. This is a statement, not a measured headroom [CP-1].

Rate-sensitive, cyclical earnings [Documentary Fact]. Gain on sale margin was 2.54% in Q3 2026 against 2.80% a year earlier, adjusted revenue has fallen each quarter of 2026, and fourth-quarter adjusted revenue is guided to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion. Rising rates reduce origination volume while raising MSR value, so earnings quality depends on valuation items the company excludes from adjusted measures [CP-1; CP-1A].

Uncommitted secured funding and renewal risk [Documentary Fact]. Secured financing of USD 14,187 million exceeds the USD 7,400 million committed secured lines, almost all of it matures in 2027 and 2028, and most facilities have cross default terms. A margin call or non-renewal would draw on cash first [CP-1 debt stack].

Agency and counterparty dependence [Documentary Fact]. Servicing and loan sales depend on Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae programmes and guidelines, and counterparties can terminate servicing. The loss of eligibility or fee cuts would hit income and MSR collateral together [CP-1A operating model].

Founder control with unseen protections [Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on protective terms]. The controlling holder, controlled company exemptions and renounced corporate opportunities limit board-level checks, and the governance letter, indentures and credit agreements that would limit owner actions are not supplied. This is a monitoring weakness, not evidence of owner extraction [CP-1A ownership and governance].

Legal and acquired-liability exposure [Documentary Fact]. Reserves of USD 216 million, a USD 175 million verdict awaiting judgment, a data breach class action inherited from Mr. Cooper and unquantified investor representation exposure form event risk that could reach liquidity through judgment thresholds [CP-1 claims outside funded debt].

Opaque debt terms and liquidity [Insufficient Information]. Covenant levels, guarantor names, per-instrument issuer roles, ratings, cash paid for interest in 2026 and the basis of USD 6.2 billion of stated secured availability are not supplied, so headroom, ranking and cash cover cannot be sized. Missing evidence is not read as adverse; it limits confidence [CP-0; CP-1; CP-1A].

Comparability and adjustments [Analyst Interpretation]. Perimeter changes, a segment recast, interest caption changes and large add-backs mean year-on-year growth mixes acquired and organic change, and revenue cannot be compared between FY2025 and 2026 captions. Credit judgments should rest on net income, adjusted EBITDA and balance sheet figures [CP-0; CP-1].

runs.text: All transactions below are completed unless stated. Figures are in US dollars in millions.

The Up-C Collapse closed on June 30, 2025. The previously outstanding Class D common shares and Holdings LLC Units were exchanged and retired for new Class L common stock, Class B and Class C stock were eliminated, and the company now holds indirectly all voting and economic interests in Rocket Limited Partnership (10-K page:140). It was accounted for as a common control transaction. The Tax Receivable Agreement was amended so that its terms do not apply to exchanges on or after March 9, 2025, including those made in the collapse (10-K page:156). Class L shares are subject to lock-up periods, with transfers barred until the first anniversary of closing and half of the shares until the second anniversary, and all Class L shares convert automatically on the later of June 30, 2027 and the date Class L falls below the stated voting share (10-K page:90). In the third quarter of 2026, 924,439,710 Class L shares were converted into Class A shares on a one-for-one basis (Q3 10-Q page:46). The filings do not say who converted them or whether any were sold; the timing follows the first anniversary of the collapse (Analyst Interpretation).

The Redfin acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective July 1, 2025 with consideration of 1,742: 1,466 of Class A stock, 24 of converted equity awards and 252 of cash that settled Redfin's term loan, accrued interest and prepayment premium. Redfin carried unsecured financing of 526 at acquisition (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). The purchase price allocation was finalised in Q2 2026 with no measurement-period adjustments. The Mr. Cooper acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective October 1, 2025 with consideration of 16,973: 13,667 of Class A stock, 193 of converted awards and 3,113 of cash that settled Mr. Cooper's unsecured senior notes, accrued interest and fees (Q3 10-Q page:17). Liabilities assumed included secured financing of 6,461 and unsecured financing of 1,956. In Q3 2026 the allocation was finalised with a 75 increase to goodwill, arising from a 100 increase in litigation and regulatory accruals offset by a 25 decrease in net deferred tax liabilities, with no earnings impact (Q3 10-Q page:18). Goodwill from the two deals is 8,326 and 1,233 and is not tax deductible (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:18). The 10-K states that revenue and net income since the acquisition dates cannot be separated (10-K page:165).

New debt in 2025: the note table lists 2,000 of 6.125% senior notes due 2030 and 2,000 of 6.375% senior notes due 2033 (10-K page:180), and the 2025 cash flow statement shows borrowings on senior notes of 4,000 (10-K page:138). An indenture dated June 20, 2025 with guarantors named therein is listed as an exhibit (10-K page:222), and the Q3 10-Q says the 4.0 billion offering completed in June 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:67). The note table footnotes instead say the offerings were completed in October 2025 (10-K page:181). This is logged as a conflict and not reconciled. Proceeds from the June 2025 issuance were used to fund the tender, redemption and consent solicitations for Nationstar notes (10-K page:165). In exchange offers, 738 of the 750 of 6.500% notes due 2029 and 955 of the 1,000 of 7.125% notes due 2032 were tendered and replaced by Rocket Companies notes, and tender offers bought 574 of 650 of 5.125% notes due 2030 and 536 of 600 of 5.750% notes due 2031. Rocket Mortgage, LLC assumed the notes not tendered. The company also redeemed 500 of 5.000% notes due 2026, 600 of 6.000% notes due 2027 and 850 of 5.500% notes due 2028 (10-K page:165 to page:166). A 364-day senior unsecured Bridge Facility is defined and its financing fees were expensed within acquisition-related expenses (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:55). The facility amount and any drawing are not printed in the pack, and it does not appear in the debt tables at either year-end or September 30, 2026.

Other 2025 capital events: the company declared a special dividend of $0.80 per Class A share on March 10, 2025 in connection with the Up-C Collapse, paid $120.1 million on April 3, 2025 (10-K page:95). It terminated two lines of credit from RHI with capacities of 2,000 and 100 in 2025, neither drawn, and terminated a surplus debenture between RHI and RTIC (10-K page:181). A Revolving Credit Agreement dated April 30, 2025 with Rocket Mortgage, LLC as borrower and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as agent is listed in the 10-K exhibits (10-K page:222).

New debt in 2026: on June 9, 2026 the company issued 1,500 of senior notes, of which 900 are 6.125% notes due 2031 and 600 are 6.500% notes due 2034; management said the offering was more than seven times oversubscribed and upsized from 1,200, and that proceeds redeemed outstanding senior notes and repaid other debt (Q2 release page:3, Management Language). The Q3 10-Q table shows the 2.875% notes due 2026 (1,150) redeemed at 100% plus about 6 of accrued interest, and the 5.250% notes due 2028 (62) redeemed at 100% plus about 2 of accrued interest (Q3 10-Q page:30 to page:31). The revolving credit facility was increased from 2,300 to 2,500, fully committed, and extended to July 16, 2029 (Q2 10-Q page:28; Q3 10-Q page:30). The Q2 and Q3 10-Q exhibit lists name a Revolving Credit Agreement dated July 16, 2026 with Rocket Companies, Inc. as Borrower, guarantors and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as agent (Q3 10-Q page:71), whereas the 2025 agreement had Rocket Mortgage, LLC as borrower. The filings do not say whether the 2026 agreement amends and restates the 2025 one; the change of borrower is an open distinction that matters for ranking. Nationstar Mortgage was merged into Rocket Mortgage in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:35). A personal loan funding facility was increased to 300 after September 30, 2026, and three repurchase facilities were extended and one matured after quarter end (Q3 10-Q page:29, Subsequent events). No debt transaction dated after the Q3 10-Q signature of October 30, 2026 is in the pack.

Liquidity effect and status: the 2025 and 2026 issuances replaced assumed and maturing notes, lengthened the revolver and left no senior note maturing before 2027 (CP-1). Total unsecured principal rose from 10,455 at December 31, 2025 to 10,743 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:30). The 2025 special dividend and RHI line terminations show owner-related cash and backstop moves before the acquisitions; no distribution to owners appears in the 2026 cash flow statements beyond distributions to other unit holders of 8 and taxes withheld on equity awards (Q3 10-Q page:7).

fields.value: Rocket Companies, Inc. is a Delaware holding company (Q3 10-Q page:1) whose subsidiaries originate and service US residential mortgages and run real estate and personal finance businesses (Q3 10-Q page:8). Its funded debt has two layers that must not be mixed. The first is unsecured corporate debt: senior notes with principal of 10,743 at September 30, 2026 and a revolving credit facility of 2,500 that is undrawn (Q3 10-Q page:30). The second is secured financing of 14,187: repurchase agreements, early funding facilities, MSR lines, advance facilities and personal loan lines, collateralized by loans held for sale, MSRs and advance receivables (Q3 10-Q page:27 to page:29). The company's adjusted EBITDA is stated after the interest on secured financing and before bond interest on the senior notes (Q3 release page:10), so the consistent leverage numerator is the unsecured debt. On that basis, unsecured debt of 10,743 over last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of 2,843 gives 3.78x, and 2.83x net of cash of 2,699. Both are computed here from printed components; no net debt or debt to EBITDA ratio is printed in any of the seven sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The direction of travel is favourable but the base is thin. The ratio on FY2025 earnings is 8.16x and on March 31, 2026 last-twelve-month earnings 5.65x, because debt already included the notes assumed from Mr. Cooper while earnings held only part of a year of that business (Mr. Cooper was acquired on October 1, 2025; Q3 10-Q page:8). Unsecured principal rose from 10,455 at December 31, 2025 to 10,743 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:30), so the improvement comes from earnings, not from debt reduction. The September 30, 2026 last-twelve-month period is the first made only of quarters that include both acquisitions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are cyclical and rate-sensitive. Adjusted revenue was 2,822 in Q1 2026, 2,761 in Q2 2026 and 2,574 in Q3 2026, and the company guides fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted revenue to between 2.1 billion and 2.3 billion (Q3 release page:3), below each of the three 2026 quarters. The Q3 10-Q ties the quarter to a rise in the 30-year mortgage rate from 6.43% in early July to 7.28% at the end of September and a smaller mortgage market than in the second quarter (Q3 10-Q page:49). GAAP net income of 709 in Q3 2026 includes a valuation gain on MSRs that the company removes from adjusted measures (710 in the adjusted revenue reconciliation, Q3 release page:6), so GAAP and adjusted earnings tell different stories and the committee should anchor on the adjusted measures with that caveat. Last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA includes three quarters of higher adjusted revenue than the guided fourth quarter, which means the 3.78x ratio is not a forward run-rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is stated by the company at 11.4 billion at September 30, 2026, made of cash of 2.7 billion, undrawn lines of credit of 2.5 billion and undrawn available MSR and advance lines of 6.2 billion (Q3 10-Q page:67). Cash of 2,699 and the undrawn revolver of 2,500 tie to the filings. The 6.2 billion does not tie to the secured financing table, which prints line amount, committed amount and outstanding balance but no availability (see Calculations). Most secured funding sits on uncommitted capacity: secured outstanding of 14,187 exceeds the committed secured line amount of 7,400 (Q3 10-Q page:29), and the 10-K flags the larger uncommitted portion of its loan funding facilities as a risk (10-K page:47). Covenants are described by type with compliance stated, and no level or headroom is printed (Q3 10-Q page:27), so covenant headroom is Not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover on a cash basis is available only for FY2025 and is mixed in basis; the quarterly reports do not print cash paid for interest. An accrual proxy, adjusted EBITDA over bond interest expense, is 4.94x for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026. The confidence in this base view is Medium: statements, debt and liquidity are well sourced, while the covenant, guarantor, rating, cash-interest and secured-availability inputs that a lender would normally use to size headroom and recovery are absent from the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rocket Companies, Inc. is a Detroit-based, Delaware-incorporated holding company that originates and services US residential mortgages and, since 2025, also runs a real estate brokerage and search platform (Redfin) and personal finance businesses (Rocket Money and Rocket Loans) (Q3 10-Q page:8; 10-K page:5 to page:7). Revenue comes from four lines: gain on sale of loans, loan servicing income, interest income and other income. For the nine months of 2026 these were 3,609, 2,236, 1,640 and 1,524, summing to total revenue, net of 9,009 (Q3 10-Q page:5). The structural change in the last eighteen months is scale and mix. The June 30, 2025 Up-C Collapse removed the paired-interest structure and left only Class A and Class L common stock (10-K page:140). Redfin (July 1, 2025) and Mr. Cooper (October 1, 2025) were both bought for stock, with 1,742 and 16,973 of consideration respectively, of which cash of 252 and 3,113 repaid target debt (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). The servicing portfolio is now 2,007,176 of unpaid principal, of which 1,201,476 is owned MSRs and 805,700 is subservicing and other (Q3 10-Q page:62).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The mechanics that matter for a creditor are these. First, revenue durability rests on servicing fee income, which was 3,181 in the nine months of 2026 and comes from a portfolio of agency and government loans serviced under contracts that the Agencies and subservicing clients can terminate on little or no notice (Q3 10-Q page:5; 10-K page:29). Second, margin resilience depends on interest rates through both channels: higher rates cut origination (the 30-year rate rose to 7.28% by the end of September 2026 and the market was smaller than in the second quarter, Q3 10-Q page:49) but raise MSR fair value, which flatters GAAP income and is removed from adjusted measures (Q3 release page:6). Third, liquidity and refinancing run through two layers: unsecured senior notes of 10,743 and an undrawn 2,500 revolver, and secured financing of 14,187, most of which sits on uncommitted lines (CP-1). Fourth, control sits with Mr. Gilbert, whose majority voting power lets the company use controlled company exemptions from independent director requirements (10-K page:86). The company renounced certain corporate opportunities in favour of RHI II parties (10-K page:83). The governance letter agreement of March 31, 2025 with Mr. Gilbert is listed as an exhibit but its terms are not in the pack (10-K page:222).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-relevant history is acquisitive and equity-funded, followed by refinancing: stock paid for both targets, 4.0 billion of senior notes were raised in 2025, Mr. Cooper's legacy notes were tendered or assumed, and in 2026 1.5 billion of new notes were issued, 1,212 of notes were redeemed and a larger, longer revolver was put in place (see the transaction section). The view is Medium confidence: the documentary base for operations and transactions is strong, while the documents that would show what owners may do with cash and collateral (indentures, credit agreements, the governance letter and the proxy statement) are absent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Up-C Collapse closed on June 30, 2025. The previously outstanding Class D common shares and Holdings LLC Units were exchanged and retired for new Class L common stock, Class B and Class C stock were eliminated, and the company now holds indirectly all voting and economic interests in Rocket Limited Partnership (10-K page:140). It was accounted for as a common control transaction. The Tax Receivable Agreement was amended so that its terms do not apply to exchanges on or after March 9, 2025, including those made in the collapse (10-K page:156). Class L shares are subject to lock-up periods, with transfers barred until the first anniversary of closing and half of the shares until the second anniversary, and all Class L shares convert automatically on the later of June 30, 2027 and the date Class L falls below the stated voting share (10-K page:90). In the third quarter of 2026, 924,439,710 Class L shares were converted into Class A shares on a one-for-one basis (Q3 10-Q page:46). The filings do not say who converted them or whether any were sold; the timing follows the first anniversary of the collapse (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Redfin acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective July 1, 2025 with consideration of 1,742: 1,466 of Class A stock, 24 of converted equity awards and 252 of cash that settled Redfin's term loan, accrued interest and prepayment premium. Redfin carried unsecured financing of 526 at acquisition (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:17). The purchase price allocation was finalised in Q2 2026 with no measurement-period adjustments. The Mr. Cooper acquisition was an all-stock transaction effective October 1, 2025 with consideration of 16,973: 13,667 of Class A stock, 193 of converted awards and 3,113 of cash that settled Mr. Cooper's unsecured senior notes, accrued interest and fees (Q3 10-Q page:17). Liabilities assumed included secured financing of 6,461 and unsecured financing of 1,956. In Q3 2026 the allocation was finalised with a 75 increase to goodwill, arising from a 100 increase in litigation and regulatory accruals offset by a 25 decrease in net deferred tax liabilities, with no earnings impact (Q3 10-Q page:18). Goodwill from the two deals is 8,326 and 1,233 and is not tax deductible (Q3 10-Q page:16 to page:18). The 10-K states that revenue and net income since the acquisition dates cannot be separated (10-K page:165).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in 2025: the note table lists 2,000 of 6.125% senior notes due 2030 and 2,000 of 6.375% senior notes due 2033 (10-K page:180), and the 2025 cash flow statement shows borrowings on senior notes of 4,000 (10-K page:138). An indenture dated June 20, 2025 with guarantors named therein is listed as an exhibit (10-K page:222), and the Q3 10-Q says the 4.0 billion offering completed in June 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:67). The note table footnotes instead say the offerings were completed in October 2025 (10-K page:181). This is logged as a conflict and not reconciled. Proceeds from the June 2025 issuance were used to fund the tender, redemption and consent solicitations for Nationstar notes (10-K page:165). In exchange offers, 738 of the 750 of 6.500% notes due 2029 and 955 of the 1,000 of 7.125% notes due 2032 were tendered and replaced by Rocket Companies notes, and tender offers bought 574 of 650 of 5.125% notes due 2030 and 536 of 600 of 5.750% notes due 2031. Rocket Mortgage, LLC assumed the notes not tendered. The company also redeemed 500 of 5.000% notes due 2026, 600 of 6.000% notes due 2027 and 850 of 5.500% notes due 2028 (10-K page:165 to page:166). A 364-day senior unsecured Bridge Facility is defined and its financing fees were expensed within acquisition-related expenses (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:55). The facility amount and any drawing are not printed in the pack, and it does not appear in the debt tables at either year-end or September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other 2025 capital events: the company declared a special dividend of $0.80 per Class A share on March 10, 2025 in connection with the Up-C Collapse, paid $120.1 million on April 3, 2025 (10-K page:95). It terminated two lines of credit from RHI with capacities of 2,000 and 100 in 2025, neither drawn, and terminated a surplus debenture between RHI and RTIC (10-K page:181). A Revolving Credit Agreement dated April 30, 2025 with Rocket Mortgage, LLC as borrower and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as agent is listed in the 10-K exhibits (10-K page:222).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt in 2026: on June 9, 2026 the company issued 1,500 of senior notes, of which 900 are 6.125% notes due 2031 and 600 are 6.500% notes due 2034; management said the offering was more than seven times oversubscribed and upsized from 1,200, and that proceeds redeemed outstanding senior notes and repaid other debt (Q2 release page:3, Management Language). The Q3 10-Q table shows the 2.875% notes due 2026 (1,150) redeemed at 100% plus about 6 of accrued interest, and the 5.250% notes due 2028 (62) redeemed at 100% plus about 2 of accrued interest (Q3 10-Q page:30 to page:31). The revolving credit facility was increased from 2,300 to 2,500, fully committed, and extended to July 16, 2029 (Q2 10-Q page:28; Q3 10-Q page:30). The Q2 and Q3 10-Q exhibit lists name a Revolving Credit Agreement dated July 16, 2026 with Rocket Companies, Inc. as Borrower, guarantors and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as agent (Q3 10-Q page:71), whereas the 2025 agreement had Rocket Mortgage, LLC as borrower. The filings do not say whether the 2026 agreement amends and restates the 2025 one; the change of borrower is an open distinction that matters for ranking. Nationstar Mortgage was merged into Rocket Mortgage in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:35). A personal loan funding facility was increased to 300 after September 30, 2026, and three repurchase facilities were extended and one matured after quarter end (Q3 10-Q page:29, Subsequent events). No debt transaction dated after the Q3 10-Q signature of October 30, 2026 is in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity effect and status: the 2025 and 2026 issuances replaced assumed and maturing notes, lengthened the revolver and left no senior note maturing before 2027 (CP-1). Total unsecured principal rose from 10,455 at December 31, 2025 to 10,743 at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:30). The 2025 special dividend and RHI line terminations show owner-related cash and backstop moves before the acquisitions; no distribution to owners appears in the 2026 cash flow statements beyond distributions to other unit holders of 8 and taxes withheld on equity awards (Q3 10-Q page:7).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rocket Companies, Inc. is a large but cyclical mortgage credit whose unsecured leverage looks moderate today and could weaken quickly if rates keep rising. The strongest support is a full post-acquisition earnings base: last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,843 million against senior notes of USD 10,743 million gives 3.78x gross and 2.83x net of USD 2,699 million of cash, with no note due before 2027 and an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver. The weakest point is dependence on mortgage rates, on USD 14,187 million of mostly uncommitted secured funding and on Agency servicing contracts, under a founder whose creditor-protection documents are not available. The outcome will be decided by whether adjusted revenue holds near the guided USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion without a funding or legal shock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rocket's unsecured leverage has fallen to a moderate level, but the improvement is earnings-led and the latest ratio is the first on a clean base. Senior notes of USD 10,743 million (principal) stand at 3.78x last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,843 million and 2.83x net of USD 2,699 million of cash, against 8.16x for FY2025 and 5.65x at March 31, 2026, when earnings held only part of the Mr. Cooper business while debt already held its assumed notes. Principal rose from USD 10,455 million at December 31, 2025, so deleveraging came from earnings, not repayment [CP-1 leverage table; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on cause].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratio flatters the forward position. Adjusted revenue fell from USD 2,822 million in Q1 2026 to USD 2,761 million in Q2 2026 and USD 2,574 million in Q3 2026, and the company guides Q4 2026 to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion, below each quarter in the last-twelve-month window. The third quarter coincided with a 30-year mortgage rate that rose from 6.43% to 7.28% and a smaller market, while GAAP net income of USD 709 million included an MSR valuation gain that the company strips out of adjusted measures. Creditors should anchor on adjusted EBITDA with that caveat and treat the 3.78x as a trailing, not forward, figure [CP-1; CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rocket's funding has two layers that behave differently. The unsecured layer, senior notes and an undrawn USD 2,500 million revolver maturing in 2029, has no maturity before the USD 503 million convertible in April 2027, then USD 1,500 million in 2029, USD 2,076 million in 2030 and USD 2,214 million in 2031. The secured layer of USD 14,187 million sits on lines whose committed amount is USD 7,400 million, with USD 10,295 million outstanding on lines dated 2027 and USD 3,462 million on lines dated 2028. Rocket therefore faces recurring renewal and margin-call risk on warehouse capacity even though its bond maturity profile is long, and most facilities carry cross default or cross acceleration terms [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is real but partly unverified. The company states total liquidity of USD 11.4 billion, of which only USD 2,699 million of cash and the USD 2,500 million revolver tie to the filings; the USD 6.2 billion of undrawn available MSR and advance lines cannot be reproduced from the facility table, and cash includes buy-down and margin cash that are not quantified. Stated liquidity is management data and should be attributed as such [CP-1; Management Language].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The servicing franchise is the most durable source of revenue and also a concentration. Servicing fee income was USD 3,181 million in the nine months of 2026 on a portfolio of USD 2,007,176 million of unpaid principal, with 60-plus day delinquency of 1.52%. The Agencies and subservicing clients can terminate servicing with little or no notice, and MSRs of USD 20,257 million at fair value are the largest balance sheet asset and are valued with rate and prepayment assumptions. A change in Agency terms or an MSR valuation reversal would hit income, collateral value for the MSR lines and liquidity at once [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control and sponsor behaviour matter because protections are not visible. Mr. Gilbert holds more than a majority of the voting power, the company relies on controlled company exemptions and renounces certain corporate opportunities in favour of RHI II parties. Documented capital actions are mixed: a USD 120.1 million special dividend in 2025, withdrawal of undrawn related party credit lines, equity-funded acquisitions and no distributions in the 2026 cash flow statements. Nothing in the pack shows the restricted payment, lien or guarantee terms that would limit owner actions [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on overall category].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Event risk is concentrated in litigation and acquired liabilities. Legal reserves rose to USD 216 million from USD 74 million, acquisition accounting added USD 100 million of litigation and regulatory accruals in Q3 2026, and a USD 175 million HouseCanary verdict against Rocket Close awaits judgment while the plaintiff is in Chapter 11. A judgment above facility thresholds that is not paid, bonded or stayed could default funding facilities, which links a legal outcome to liquidity [CP-1 claims outside funded debt; Documentary Fact].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings carry adjustments and a definition that favours the headline. Adjusted EBITDA is after secured financing interest but before bond interest, adds back USD 291 million of acquisition-related expenses and USD 338 million of acquired intangible amortization in the nine months, and removes an MSR valuation gain of USD 852 million. Accrual cover of last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA over bond interest is 4.94x, and cash interest cover is available only for FY2025 at 2.15x on a mixed basis. Debt service capacity therefore rests on an accrual proxy and on adjusted rather than reported earnings [CP-1 earnings quality; Analyst Interpretation].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Market pricing of the unsecured notes weakened over the period. The aggregate fair value of senior notes of USD 10,258 million at September 30, 2026 was below carrying value of USD 10,716 million, whereas at December 31, 2025 fair value of USD 10,502 million was above carrying value of USD 10,423 million, and the weighted average interest rate on the notes rose to 5.43% from 5.03%. This is an aggregate, not a tranche-level price, and ratings are not supplied [CP-1 debt stack; Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation on direction].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scaled servicing and origination franchise [Documentary Fact]. Rocket Companies, Inc. services USD 2,007,176 million of unpaid principal, earned USD 3,181 million of servicing fee income in the nine months of 2026 and closed USD 43.6 billion of loans in Q3 2026. Recurring servicing fees support revenue visibility through a rate cycle better than origination alone, and the portfolio's 60-plus day delinquency of 1.52% is stable against 1.50% at year end [CP-1A operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Moderate unsecured leverage on a full earnings base [Documentary Fact]. Gross 3.78x and net 2.83x on last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, with accrual bond interest cover of 4.94x, give room to absorb some earnings decline before leverage reaches the 5.65x seen at March 31, 2026 [CP-1 leverage table; Analyst Interpretation on headroom].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Long unsecured maturity profile and an undrawn revolver [Documentary Fact]. No note matures before April 2027, the largest annual maturities fall in 2031 and 2033, and the USD 2,500 million revolver is undrawn and runs to 2029, which gives the issuer time and a committed buffer [CP-1 debt maturities; CP-1 liquidity table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity-funded growth [Documentary Fact]. Redfin and Mr. Cooper were bought for stock, with cash of USD 252 million and USD 3,113 million used to settle target debt, so the acquisitions did not require a new debt-funded purchase price. Equity of USD 24,311 million and equity less goodwill and intangibles of USD 11,745 million (a consolidated proxy, not a covenant measure) provide loss-absorbing capital for the debt [CP-1A transactions; CP-1 financials].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Stated compliance [Documentary Fact]. The company states compliance with all funding covenants and with agency net worth, liquidity and capital ratio requirements at September 30, 2026. This is a statement, not a measured headroom [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rate-sensitive, cyclical earnings [Documentary Fact]. Gain on sale margin was 2.54% in Q3 2026 against 2.80% a year earlier, adjusted revenue has fallen each quarter of 2026, and fourth-quarter adjusted revenue is guided to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.3 billion. Rising rates reduce origination volume while raising MSR value, so earnings quality depends on valuation items the company excludes from adjusted measures [CP-1; CP-1A].

fields.value: Uncommitted secured funding and renewal risk [Documentary Fact]. Secured financing of USD 14,187 million exceeds the USD 7,400 million committed secured lines, almost all of it matures in 2027 and 2028, and most facilities have cross default terms. A margin call or non-renewal would draw on cash first [CP-1 debt stack].

fields.value: Agency and counterparty dependence [Documentary Fact]. Servicing and loan sales depend on Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae programmes and guidelines, and counterparties can terminate servicing. The loss of eligibility or fee cuts would hit income and MSR collateral together [CP-1A operating model].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Founder control with unseen protections [Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on protective terms]. The controlling holder, controlled company exemptions and renounced corporate opportunities limit board-level checks, and the governance letter, indentures and credit agreements that would limit owner actions are not supplied. This is a monitoring weakness, not evidence of owner extraction [CP-1A ownership and governance].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legal and acquired-liability exposure [Documentary Fact]. Reserves of USD 216 million, a USD 175 million verdict awaiting judgment, a data breach class action inherited from Mr. Cooper and unquantified investor representation exposure form event risk that could reach liquidity through judgment thresholds [CP-1 claims outside funded debt].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opaque debt terms and liquidity [Insufficient Information]. Covenant levels, guarantor names, per-instrument issuer roles, ratings, cash paid for interest in 2026 and the basis of USD 6.2 billion of stated secured availability are not supplied, so headroom, ranking and cash cover cannot be sized. Missing evidence is not read as adverse; it limits confidence [CP-0; CP-1; CP-1A].

fields.value: Comparability and adjustments [Analyst Interpretation]. Perimeter changes, a segment recast, interest caption changes and large add-backs mean year-on-year growth mixes acquired and organic change, and revenue cannot be compared between FY2025 and 2026 captions. Credit judgments should rest on net income, adjusted EBITDA and balance sheet figures [CP-0; CP-1].
